gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'boost' ratings on 1 kWh stations are reduced-voltage modes and not extra continuous power. EcoFlow's X-Boost (2,200 W on the DELTA 3) 'marginally reduces voltage', and BLUETTI limits the AC180's 2,700 W Power Lifting mode to 'pure-resistive heating devices', so for a microwave the continuous AC rating is the real ceiling. Only the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 has 2,000 W of continuous output with no boost mode involved.
standout_why: I compared against the cited KeepLights microwave guide, the cited PowerStationTips runtime article, Wattcellar (the top non-Dealectric result) and our own page. KeepLights says only that EcoFlow's X-Boost on the RIVER 2 Pro 'names a microwave as one use' and leaves it out of the math. It does not say how X-Boost works and does not mention BLUETTI Power Lifting or Anker SurgePad. PowerStationTips says a surge rating is 'a non-issue for microwaves' and that transformer microwaves cycle 'at full input'. Wattcellar mentions no boost modes. Our page says to use 'a smaller microwave… not a power-saving mode' but gives no maker wording or mechanism. None of the pages states BLUETTI's resistive-only limit or EcoFlow's reduced-voltage wording.
decides: This confirms the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 as the pick for full-size microwaves drawing about 1,600–2,000 W. Its 2,000 W is a plain continuous rating. The BLUETTI AC180's 2,700 W covers resistive heating devices only, so the AC180 stays capped at 1,800 W for a microwave. The DELTA 3's 2,200 W comes only in X-Boost, which runs at reduced voltage. EcoFlow lists a 1,300 W microwave as an X-Boost example, but that is already below the DELTA 3's 1,800 W continuous rating. So the boost figures should not be used to move the line for the microwave sizes each station can run.

findings.label: What Power Lifting mode is for
findings.value: AC output boosted to 2,700 W, 'Ideal for pure-resistive heating devices, such as hair dryers, electric kettles, heaters, etc.' Rated output is 1,800 W continuous.
findings.note: This is BLUETTI's Canadian page for the same 120 V AC180, used because the US page returned HTTP 429. It does not mention microwaves among Power Lifting loads.

findings.label: How X-Boost works, in EcoFlow's words
findings.value: 'an intelligent voltage control that marginally reduces voltage' so you can 'power devices with a lower-rated inverter'. Lists a microwave (1,300 W) as an example. Not available while the station is charging.
findings.note: The page does not say how much power reaches the appliance at the reduced voltage. It warns that with several devices 'the change of voltage may affect device usage performance'.

findings.label: AC output, X-Boost and price
findings.value: 1,800 W continuous; 2,200 W with X-Boost (3,600 W surge); $579.00

findings.label: AC output, X-Boost claim and price
findings.value: 1,800 W continuous, 3,600 W surge; X-Boost 'supports high-demand devices up to 2600W such as microwaves'; $459.00
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic Portable Power Station (1024Wh)
findings.note: EcoFlow names microwaves as an X-Boost load, which conflicts with BLUETTI limiting its boost mode to resistive heating. The X-Boost figure is a reduced-voltage mode, not continuous power.

findings.label: AC output on Anker US page
findings.value: 2,000 W max continuous (120 V, 16.66 A); 3,000 W peak; SurgePad not mentioned
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen2 - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: The spec lists '120V~ 16.66A, 60Hz, 2,000W Max'. The page says 3,000 W peak 'handles sudden power surges'. No boost mode is needed to reach 2,000 W.

findings.label: SurgePad rating (Gen 1)
findings.value: 1,800 W inverter output; SurgePad 'up to 2400W'; bypass 1,440 W
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Portable Power Station
findings.note: The SurgePad section lists kettles, heaters, a griddle and a hair dryer, and no microwave. Anker gives no mechanism or duration for SurgePad.
